L2 delivered: per-seat and pooled dependency-edge trigger counts, trigger rate with Wilson interval over the block-level denominators; if two-digit triggers are NOT reached, the reading says so and delivers the interval, never a rate dressed as a conclusion

L6 delivered: replanning effectiveness on the model seat at the block-level denominators AND on the rule seat's 60 zero-cost episodes at the same episode denominator, side by side, same denominator per seat
L2's rule-seat status restated (v0.3: structurally n/m) with whatever the 60 rule episodes show
every non-success row in the errors ledger (v0.4 R1), every block manifest carrying its perception channel and model identity (v0.4 R2)
the two-ledger spend reported with http_requests and http_requests_successful side by side (batch_spend)
seat identity per block in the state file; the pooled reading stratifies by seat wherever seats differ

block_plan.checkpoint: a kill loses at most the block in flight; a restart resumes at the next unfinished block, re-running no paid episode
block_plan.seat_fallback: blocks run on the primary seat; if the stop rule trips at a block boundary, the NEXT block may switch to the failover seat (recorded per block, reading stratified). The switch exists to preserve the denominator under quota pressure, not to halve wall clock: blocks are sequential because the experience store is batch-level state

cost.basis: v0.3 E1 measured 31.1 requests per lh episode all-in (v0.4 phase log P2-E, batch_spend over the lh cells)
cost.rule_seat_half: 0 requests: the L6 cross-seat counterpart is a rule-planner run of the same set x arm x repeats, paid in wall clock only
cost.stop_rule: 3 consecutive 429/quota deaths -> stop at the block boundary, checkpoint, log; bound hit -> stop, no 'a little more'; a resumed block re-runs no paid episode

credentials: never recorded; a config names the env var, not the key (SPEC 7)

design.planner: deepseek (bst_text_agnes.yaml), the seat that carried E1's 2,936 requests
design.store: per-cell experience store and skill library, fresh files, shared across blocks in set order (the same growth one continuous 60-episode run would produce)

experiment: E1' (v0.4) — L2/L6 denominators raised to conclusion-grade scale (RQ9, SPEC v0.4 §7 E1')

scale_rationale: D5' (user, 2026-09-30): 60 episodes targets two-digit L2 triggers at the observed 2/12 trigger rate (expected ~10); 24 was the smaller option and was declined; L2's denominator is TRIGGER SETS, not episodes, so the reading must name both
seat_plan_note: the two-seat rotation discussed at D5' was narrowed to failover-only before the first request: alternating seats would split the ~10 expected L2 triggers into per-seat halves and defeat the scale objective the batch exists for. The narrowing is recorded here rather than discovered in the report.
